args.title: Use local timezone date for export file names instead of UTC
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

Change the export file name generation to use the local timezone date, not the UTC date, so that the file name shown matches the user's date of export, fixing the issue where exports in the evening appear with the next day's date.

label: bug
file: src/exportUtils.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The export file names currently use the UTC date, causing evening exports to be named with the next day. This happens because formatExportFilename uses Date.toISOString() which is UTC. Changing to use the local date fixes the reported problem for users exporting late in the day in their own timezone.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Transaction amounts are stored as 64-bit integers in the database (Postgres bigint), representing values exactly with no rounding errors from floating point. The amounts keep their precision exactly. Currencies like the yen, which have no cents, are handled by storing whole number amounts, so no fractional values are involved.

args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

Fix the duplicate report name truncation when the report has a name close to the 120-character limit. The code truncated before appending ` (copy)`, resulting in a clipped name ending with `...`. Change to append `(copy)` properly and then truncate to ensure uniqueness in report listing.

label: bug
file: src/api/reports.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The issue is in the duplicate report endpoint where the name is truncated before adding ` (copy)`. This causes names close to the max length to end in `...` rather than having a `(copy)` suffix. Adjusting the truncation order fixes the problem, making duplicates clearly named in the reports list.

args.title: Preserve Greek and Cyrillic characters in export file names
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

Modify the export filename generation to keep Greek, Cyrillic, and other non-Latin characters in report names instead of using slugify, which strips these letters. This will ensure that export filenames preserve non-Latin alphabets, fixing the reported problem of losing original letters in exports from those reports.

label: feature
file: src/exportUtils.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Currently the export filenames use slugify which drops accents and replaces non-ASCII letters. This removes Greek and Cyrillic letters from report names in filenames. Changing to preserve original Unicode characters in filenames will keep report names recognizable in exports for these alphabets.
